correctness.rationale: Theorem is proved for every n>=3 and t>0 by strictly convex inverse-Laplacian trace, edge-injective Laplacian map and prism symmetries, exact two-mode eigenvalue decomposition, strictly decreasing root-price equation with appropriate endpoints, and uniformly controlled n^(-2/3) asymptotic minimizers. Poisson kernel yields exact resolvent sum; exact rational tests independently reconstructed matrices. Finite checker cannot prove the infinite statements.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The prism is also called a circular ladder or Cartesian product C_n square K_2, and Kirchhoff index is total pairwise effective resistance. Examined papers treat precisely those graph aliases but assume unit conductances and calculate fixed-network invariants. Our theorem optimizes every edge conductance under a two-price constraint, supplies exact unique optimum, and proves fractional scaling; those claims are neither equivalent to nor stated by the fixed-weight formulas.

originality.rationale: Complete price-dependent conductance classification and n^(-2/3) optimum-ratio law for prism networks are not entailed by the general convex optimization theorem nor by inspected unit-conductance prism Kirchhoff formulas. Checked the full 2006/2008 Ghosh-Boyd-Saberi work and primary full text of Cinkir 2017, Baigonakova-Mednykh 2019 and Azimi-Farrokhi 2023; targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no dominating exact specialization. Residual risk exists for historical less discoverable work and inaccessible full text of Carmona et al. 2014.
residual_risks: No result database or public literature search exhaustively rules out equivalent older prism optimization results, including obscure or differently named treatments.
The 2014 Carmona-Encinas-Mitjana weighted linear-chain full text was inaccessible; interpretation is restricted to verified abstract, not a full-text assertion.
General convex methods or graph spectral identities might allow a knowledgeable reader to derive the theorem but do not themselves state its optimized asymptotic.

value.rationale: A motivated exact budget allocation across two types of prism edges is solved for arbitrary network size and price. The unusual n^(-2/3) rung-to-rim law, vanishing optimal rung budget share, and explicit noninteger second-order resistance term give a structurally meaningful asymptotic prediction not present in fixed-weight Kirchhoff tabulations; not an arbitrary numerical slice.
